definitions.explanation: A flat-bodied fish that lies on the ocean floor with both eyes on one side. Prized in Japanese cuisine for its delicate white flesh, especially as sashimi and sushi.

examples.japanese: ヒラメの{刺身|さしみ}は{美味|おい}しい。
ヒラメは{高級|こうきゅう}な{白身魚|しろみざかな}として{知|し}られている。
examples.english: Flounder is known as a high-quality white fish.

examples.japanese: {寿司屋|すしや}でヒラメの{縁側|えんがわ}を{注文|ちゅうもん}したら{絶品|ぜっぴん}だった。
examples.english: When I ordered the flounder fin edge at the sushi restaurant, it was exquisite.

notes:
USAGE:
A prized sushi and sashimi fish. ヒラメ is particularly valued for its {縁側|えんがわ} (the fin edge), which has a distinctive crunchy texture.

ヒラメ VS. カレイ:
Both are flatfish, but they are different species. The saying 「{左|ひだり}ヒラメに{右|みぎ}カレイ」 (flounder on the left, sole on the right) helps distinguish them: when the belly faces you, ヒラメ has its eyes on the left side and カレイ on the right.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ヒラメの{刺身|さしみ} (flounder sashimi)
- ヒラメの{煮付|につ}け (simmered flounder)
- ヒラメの{縁側|えんがわ} (flounder fin edge — a delicacy)
- {天然|てんねん}ヒラメ (wild-caught flounder)

WRITING:
Usually written in katakana. The kanji {鮃|ひらめ} exists but is rare outside specialized contexts.
